questions.question: What was the capital of the Byzantine Empire for most of its history?
choices: Rome
Constantinople
Baghdad
Alexandria

questions.question: The Byzantine Empire developed from the eastern portion of
choices: the Persian Empire
the Mongol Empire
the Roman Empire
the Carolingian Empire

questions.question: What was the Justinian Code?
choices: A trade agreement between Byzantium and China
A list of Islamic pilgrimage sites
A system of Inca record keeping
A compilation and organization of Roman laws under Emperor Justinian

questions.question: Why was Constantinople a strategically important city?
choices: It connected trade routes between Europe and Asia and controlled access between seas
It was located in the Sahara far from trade
It had no natural harbor or defenses
It was the capital of the Song dynasty

questions.question: Which architectural landmark was first built as a Byzantine cathedral under Justinian?
choices: The Parthenon
Hagia Sophia
The Dome of the Rock
The Colosseum

questions.question: What event is commonly associated with the formal split between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches?
choices: The Council of Nicaea
The fall of the Western Roman Empire
The Great Schism of 1054
The beginning of the Crusades

questions.question: Where did Islam originate in the seventh century?
choices: The Iberian Peninsula
The Indus Valley
The Scandinavian Peninsula
The Arabian Peninsula

questions.question: What is the Qur'an in Islam?
choices: The central sacred text of Islam
A Byzantine law code
A Persian royal title
A trade route across the Sahara

questions.question: Why did cities such as Baghdad become important centers of learning in parts of the medieval Islamic world?
choices: They prohibited the study of mathematics
They supported scholarship, translation, trade, and exchange of ideas
They were isolated from trade routes
They replaced every other capital in the region

questions.question: Which institution is associated with scholarly activity in Abbasid Baghdad?
choices: The University of Bologna
The Library of Alexandria under Ptolemy
The House of Wisdom
The Royal Society

questions.question: Merchants traveling across Afro-Eurasian trade networks helped spread
choices: only one language and religion
a single political government
the same climate in every region
goods, technologies, and ideas among regions

questions.question: How did the Byzantine Empire preserve aspects of classical learning?
choices: Through the use and transmission of Greek and Roman texts and traditions
By banning all written works
By replacing every text with oral law
By isolating itself from neighboring societies

questions.question: A historian studying medieval trade finds coins from several regions in one port city. What is a reasonable conclusion?
choices: The coins prove one empire controlled every region
The city participated in long-distance exchange networks
The city had no local economy
The coins establish the exact number of merchants

questions.question: What was one effect of the expansion of Islamic caliphates in the centuries after Islam began?
choices: Every region adopted identical customs immediately
Trade ended between the Mediterranean and Asia
New political territories became connected through administration and trade, with varied local societies
The Byzantine Empire disappeared in the seventh century

questions.question: Why is it more accurate to speak of diverse societies within the medieval Islamic world than one uniform culture?
choices: Islamic societies existed only in one city
Trade prevented cultural interaction
Every caliph ruled all Muslim communities in the same way
Peoples across a wide region had varied languages, traditions, and political histories

questions.question: Which challenge contributed to the Byzantine Empire's decline before Constantinople fell in 1453?
choices: Military pressures, territorial losses, and economic strain over time
The empire had no capital city
The empire never faced external rivals
The empire lost control of the Atlantic Ocean

questions.question: Which city was captured by Ottoman forces in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire?
choices: Carthage
Constantinople
Cordoba
Damascus

questions.question: What does the term caliphate refer to in Islamic history?
choices: A specific type of Byzantine church
A law code written by Justinian
A political community or state led by a caliph
A medieval European guild

questions.question: Why did translation movements matter in medieval scholarly centers?
choices: They prevented scholars from building on earlier work
They replaced all local education
They ended trade in books and manuscripts
They helped transmit and develop knowledge across languages and regions

questions.question: A map shows the Byzantine Empire centered around Constantinople and nearby sea routes. What geographic advantage does this reveal?
choices: The city could connect commerce and military movement between several regions
The empire was separated from all maritime activity
The capital controlled the source of the Nile
The city was surrounded by uninhabitable desert
